decision: Which approach best resolves: WF-070 gates a buyer link behind an NDA. A viewer's acceptance is recorded against their own viewer session. The research states that the gate flag and the agreement id live on the Link row and that content loads only after acceptance, and it is silent on what happens when the seller amends the agreement text after a viewer has already accepted it. Which binding should a content release require?

state.problem: WF-070 gates a buyer link behind an NDA. A viewer's acceptance is recorded against their own viewer session. The research states that the gate flag and the agreement id live on the Link row and that content loads only after acceptance, and it is silent on what happens when the seller amends the agreement text after a viewer has already accepted it. Which binding should a content release require?

candidate_solutions.digest_and_id: Release content only against an acceptance whose agreement_id matches AND whose recorded digest of the text the viewer read still matches a digest of the current body (whitespace-normalised). Amending the text re-opens the gate for everyone who has not accepted the new wording. Prior acceptances are kept, each naming the version it was given under.
candidate_solutions.id_only: Release content against any acceptance naming the agreement the link points at, whatever the text said at the time. Amending the agreement does not re-open the gate.

context.workflow: WF-070 require NDA acceptance before viewing
context.research: Papermark OpenAPI CreateLinkRequest.enable_agreement: 'Require viewers to accept an agreement (NDA) before viewing. Set together with agreement_id.' agreement_id: 'ID of the Agreement viewers must accept. Required when enable_agreement is true.' CLI: '--agreement <id> ... The single flag both enables the gate and sets the agreement id'; '--enable-agreement <on|off> | Toggle the agreement (NDA) gate.'
context.implemented: backend/dsr/link_gating/agreement.py: body_digest, acceptance_covers, agreement_changes (moves version only on a real text change), and AgreementEngine.content (fails closed, distinguishes REASON_SUPERSEDED from REASON_NOT_ACCEPTED). backend/dsr/features/wf070_require_nda_acceptance_before_viewing.py exposes PATCH /links/{id}/agreement and PATCH /agreements/{id}.
context.tests: 82 domain tests and 36 HTTP tests in backend/tests/test_wf070.py and backend/tests/test_wf070_http.py. Among them: test_editing_the_nda_re_opens_the_gate_for_someone_who_already_accepted, test_pointing_a_link_at_a_different_agreement_does_not_release_it, test_fixing_a_title_does_not_move_the_version, test_whitespace_is_not_a_change_to_the_text, and test_editing_the_nda_over_http_re_opens_the_gate.
context.cost_of_digest_and_id: A cosmetic re-wrap of the same paragraphs does not re-open the gate, because whitespace is normalised before hashing. Any other edit does, so a seller who changes their terms must re-collect acceptances.
context.cost_of_id_only: Cheaper to operate. But it makes a seller's edit to their own legal text the one change that silently weakens a gate already in force, and it lets a viewer who accepted one version read a different version as if they had agreed to it.
